claims.text: `pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
The Pulumi CLI supports the command `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345` to import an AWS VPC resource.
The Pulumi CLI supports the command `pulumi import aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet private-subnet-1 subnet-67890` to import an AWS subnet resource.
The Pulumi CLI supports the command `pulumi import aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster app-cluster my-cluster` to import an AWS ECS cluster resource.
The `@pulumi/policy` package exports a `PolicyPack` construct and a `validateResourceOfType` function.
The `@pulumi/policy` `validateResourceOfType` function can be used with `aws.ec2.Instance` to validate resource properties and call `reportViolation`.
The `aws.ec2.Instance` resource exposes a `tags` property.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource exposes an `acl` property that can take values such as `public-read` or `public-read-write`.
Pulumi's Automation API is importable via `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`.
The Pulumi Automation API's `LocalWorkspace` class provides a `createOrSelectStack` method that accepts `stackName`, `projectName`, and `program` arguments.
The Pulumi Automation API stack object provides a `setConfig` method that can set configuration values such as `aws:region`.
The Pulumi Automation API stack object provides an `up` method that accepts an `onOutput` callback option.
Pulumi's `pulumi.ComponentResource` class can be extended to create custom reusable components.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` subclasses call `super()` with a type token, name, args object, and options.
The `aws.lb.LoadBalancer` resource accepts `name`, `loadBalancerType`, `subnets`, and `internal` arguments.
The `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` resource accepts `family`, `networkMode`, `requiresCompatibilities`, `cpu`, `memory`, and `containerDefinitions` arguments.
The `aws.ecs.Service` resource accepts `cluster`, `taskDefinition`, `desiredCount`, `launchType`, and `networkConfiguration` arguments.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` subclasses call a `registerOutputs` method to register component outputs.

The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide teaches readers to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi when beneficial, and orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Pulumi's `pulumi.StackReference` class provides a `getOutput` method to retrieve outputs from another stack.
There exists a `terraform.state.S3Reference` construct in a `@pulumi/terraform` package that accepts `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3.
